answers.explanation: Hubs share one collision domain and repeat everything to everyone.
A separate broadcast domain, and a router or firewall deciding what crosses it.
Two links between the same switches form a loop. STP blocks one until the other fails.
Physical separation is stronger, so it's kept for the most sensitive systems.
802.1Q adds a 4-byte tag carrying the VLAN ID.
PoE sends power down the same cable as the data.
Radio leaks past walls; a cable has to be physically reached.
A switch gives every desk its own port and collision domain at line speed. Bridges only make sense to join two existing segments.
